chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUdhāfir, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a man: is his wudu (ablution) invalidated when he sleeps while sitting? He said: If it is on the day of الجمعة, then there is no wudu upon him, and that is because he is in a state of necessity. So this report is to be understood to mean that there is no wudu upon him, but tayammum is upon him, because that which invalidates wudu (ablution) is not specific to the day of الجمعة to the exclusion of other days. Thus, the correct understanding in it is that he performs tayammum and offers salat (prayer), then when the gathering disperses he performs wudu (ablution) and repeats the salat (prayer), because he may not have been able to get out due to the crowding. And that which indicates this is what...

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمُ: tayammum, dry ablution required when ordinary wudu (ablution) cannot be performed
key_terms.الزَّحْمَةِ: crowding, the practical obstacle preventing departure
key_terms.الْجَمْعُ: the gathering, referring to the congregational assembly
key_terms.حَالِ ضَرُورَةٍ: a state of necessity, the reason given for the exceptional treatment
key_terms.نَامَ: slept, the act being examined as a nullifier of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.وُضُوؤُهُ: his wudu (ablution), the state of ritual purity under discussion
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of الجمعة, the specific circumstance mentioned in the report

ai.seo_question: Does sleeping while seated invalidate wudu (ablution) on the day of الجمعة?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on sleep while seated and its effect on wudu (ablution), especially in the circumstance of الجمعة congestion. The text explains that the report is understood in light of necessity: one unable to leave due to crowding performs tayammum and salat (prayer), then later performs wudu (ablution) and repeats the prayer.
